title: Italy's cybersecurity agency ACN warns of serious risks from agentic AI, ANSA reports
date_note: ANSA's article is dated 24 November and gives no earlier date for the alert.
geo_basis: national agency; ANSA's article is datelined Rome
summary: ANSA reports that Italy's national cybersecurity agency ACN has issued an alert on the serious risks of agentic AI, which it says exposes organisations and critical infrastructure to new risk scenarios. ACN says it has detected compromise campaigns using autonomous agents, and that attackers use agentic frameworks and AI to exploit critical vulnerabilities quickly. Its advice includes updating, isolating or disconnecting outdated exposed systems and applying least privilege.
plain: Italy's cyber agency warns that autonomous AI agents are being used in attacks that run fast and continuously. It urges organisations to patch or isolate exposed systems and limit account privileges.
exec: Italy's national cyber agency says agentic AI attacks exploit critical flaws quickly and threaten critical infrastructure.
action: ACN advises updating, isolating or disconnecting exposed systems that lack the latest version, inventorying internet-facing assets, applying least privilege and monitoring for abnormal behaviour.

validation.note: Only ANSA's report was read (L'Adige and Alto Adige carry the same agency text); ACN's own alert page on its website was not read. ACN's statements are as ANSA relays them.
